item.title: Local-Cohen-Macaulay DG-rings with unequal finitistic projective dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.31392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every pair of integers $d,n\geq1$, we construct a commutative noetherian local-Cohen-Macaulay DG-ring $A$ such that $\dim H^0(A)=d$, $\mathrm{amp}(A)=n$, $\mathrm{fpd}(A)=d-n$, and $\mathrm{FPD}(A)=d$. This gives a negative answer to the implication from local-Cohen-Macaulayness to equality of the two finitistic projective dimensions in a question of Bird, Shaul, Sridhar, and Williamson.
item.dc:creator: Luigi Ferraro

item.title: Leafrians, Poisson structures, and Frobenius splittings on moduli spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.31619v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Poisson $T$-Pfaffians of Bott--Samelson varieties, $G/U$, and $G/B$ produce Frobenius splittings, but only by a local, coordinate-bound argument. We isolate the local mechanism: a weighted trace pairing on the deformation space of a fat point, whose top coefficient factors over the blocks. At the members of a presentation, polyvector fields on the base $X$ transfer to the moduli space $M$. Applied to a Poisson bivector, this produces a Poisson bivector, extending Bottacin's structure from surfaces to arbitrary dimension. Applied to a top degree polyvector $s$ and wedged with a transverse Euler frame, it produces an anticanonical section on $M$, which we call the \emph{leafrian}. When $X$ is a Poisson surface, we prove that the leafrian splits the moduli of stable sheaves, of principal $G$-bundles, and of instantons if and only if $s$ Frobenius-splits the base. The mechanism itself is dimension-free. The construction also recovers and generalizes the splittings of the Lie-theoretic examples: the $r$-matrix need not satisfy the classical Yang--Baxter equation.
item.dc:creator: Jun Peng

item.title: Homological subsets of Spec
item.description: arXiv:1701.03001v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We recover some data of a module $M$ from the Ext-family $\{Ext^i_R(M,R)\}$. In this regard, we investigate homological subsets of $Spec(R)$, defined by the help of Ext-family. For example, we present a situation for which $\bigcup_{i=0}^\infty Ass(Ext^i_R(M,R))$ is infinite, thereby answering a question of Vasconcelos. We extend Grothendieck's calculation of $dim(Ext^g_R(M,R))$ and present some new situations to calculate $dim(Ext^\ast_R(M,R))$. Also, we compute support and the set of all associated prime ideals of the Ext-family in a serial of nontrivial cases.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Asgharzadeh

item.title: On Stanley-Reisner Rings with Minimal Betti Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2603.25540v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study simplicial complexes with a given number of vertices whose Stanley-Reisner ring has the minimal sum of Betti numbers. We prove that every full subcomplex of them is homotopy equivalent either to a point or to a sphere. Moreover, we prove that such kind of simplicial complexes coincide with those having minimal Taylor resolutions.
item.dc:creator: Pimeng Dai, Li Yu

item.title: Maximal common divisors in monoid algebras
item.description: arXiv:2609.18947v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A commutative cancellative monoid has the MCD property if every nonempty finite subset has a maximal common divisor, and it has the MCD-finite property if every such subset has only finitely many maximal common divisors up to associates. We study these properties in monoid algebras. We first identify atomic and antimatter families of rank-$1$ torsion-free MCD monoids. We then prove that, for a field $F$ and a torsion-free monoid $M$, the MCD property ascends from $M$ to $F[M]$ whenever the group algebra $F[\mathcal{G}(M)]$ satisfies the ascending chain condition on principal ideals ($\mathcal{G}(M)$ denotes the Grothendieck group of $M$). We also record the pre-Schreier case as a consequence of classical GCD ascent. In contrast, for every prime $p$, we construct a reduced rank-$3$ MCD monoid $M$ such that $\mathbb{F}_p[M]$ is not an MCD domain, and an atomic rank-$1$ MCD monoid whose algebra over $\mathbb{F}_p$ is not atomic. We further prove that the prime reciprocal monoids considered here are MCD-finite and that MCD-finiteness ascends to polynomial extensions. Finally, for every prime $p$, we construct a rank-$1$ torsion-free q-GCD monoid whose algebra over $\mathbb{F}_p$ is not q-GCD, where the q-GCD property requires at most one maximal common divisor up to associates for every nonempty finite subset.
item.dc:creator: Grant Blitz, Felix Gotti, Darren Han, Hengrui Liang

item.title: Strong Lefschetz property of the Kirchhoff algebra of the complete tripartite graph $K_{1,1,n}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.21217v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: By Whitney's 2-isomorphism theorem, the cycle matroids of two graphs are isomorphic if and only if one graph can be transformed into the other by finitely many applications of two operations: separation or identification at a cut-vertex, and twisting. The complete tripartite graph whose vertex set is the disjoint union of two singletons and an $n$-element set is invariant, up to isomorphism, under these operations. In this paper we prove that the Macaulay inverse system (the Kirchhoff algebra) determined by the basis generating polynomial of the cycle matroid of such a graph has the strong Lefschetz property over a field of characteristic $0$. The proof reduces the non-degeneracy of the higher Hessians to the ranks of disjointness matrices of families of subsets (the Gottlieb--Wilson theorem) and to the representation theory of the symmetric group in relation to the Johnson scheme.
item.dc:creator: Yohji Akama
